title: Short title and commencement:
content: (1) The name of this Act is 'Right to Information Act, 2064 B.S. (2007 A.D.). (2) This Act will come into force from the 30th (Thirty) day of certification.

title: Definition:
content: Unless the subject or context otherwise requires, in this Act: (a) By "Public Body" means the body and institution according to the following list: (1) A body under the constitution, (2) A body established by the Act, (3) A body formed by the Government of Nepal, (4) Public service providing institution or foundation established by the law, Right to Information Act, 2007 (5) Political Party or organisation registered under the prevalent law. (6) Organised institution under the full or partial ownership or under control of the Government of Nepal or organized body receiving grants from the Government of Nepal, (7) Organised institution formed by the Bodies established by the Government of Nepal or the law entering into an agreement, (8) Non-Governmental Organisation/Institutions operated by obtaining money directly or indirectly from the Government of Nepal or Foreign Government or International Organisations/Institutions, (9) Other Bodies or Institution prescribed as Public Body by the Government of Nepal by publishing notice in the Gazette. (b) "Information" means any written document, material, or information related to the functions, proceedings thereof or decision of public importance made by the Public Bodies. (c) "Public Importance" means a subject related directly or indirectly witht the interest of citizens. (d) "Written Document" means any kind of scripted written document and the word shall also mean any audio visual materials collected and updated through any medium or that can be printed or retrieved. (e) "Right to Information" means the right to request and obtain information of public importance held in the Public Bodies and this term shall also include the right to study or observation of any written document, material held in Public Body or proceedings of such Public Body; to obtain a verified copy of such document, to visit or observe the place where any construction of public importance is going on and to obtain verified sample of any materials or to obtain information held in any type of machine through such machine. (f) "Information Authority" means a person appointed in accordance with Section 6. (g) "Chief" means the Chief of Public Body. Right to Information Act, 2007 (h) "Commission" means the National Information Commission constituted in accordance with Section 11. (i) "Chief Information Commissioner" means the person appointed in accordance with Section 11. (j) "Information Commissioner" means the person appointed accordance with Section 11. (k) "Prescribed" or "As prescribed" means prescribed or as prescribed in Rules framed under this Act. Chapter- Two Right to Information and Provision Regarding the Flow of Information

title: Right to Information:
content: (1) Every citizen shall have the right to information subject to this Act. (2) Every citizen shall have access to the information held iin the public Bodies. (3) Notwithstanding anything provided in Sections (1) and (2), the information held by the Public Bodies on the following subject matters will not be released: (a) which seriously jeopardizes the sovereignty, integrity, national security, public peace, stability and international relations of Nepal. (b) which directly affects the investigation, inquiry and prosecution of crimes. (c) having serious impact on the protection of economic, trade or monetary interest or intellectual property or banking or trade privacy. (d) that jeopardizes the harmonious relationship subsisted among various cast or communities. Right to Information Act, 2007 (e) that interferes on individual privacy and security of body, life, property or health of a person. Provided that, public Body shall not refrain from the responsibility of flowing information without appropriate and adequate reason not to flow information. (4) If a Public Body has both the information in its record that can be made public and that cannot be made public in accordance with this Act, the Information Officer shall have to provide information to the application after separating the information which can be made public.

title: Responsibility of Public Body:
content: (1) Every Public Body has to respect and protect the right to information of citizen. (2) Public Body shall have following responsibilities for the purpose of Sub- Section (1): (a) to classify and update information and make them public, publish and broadcast, (b) to make the citizens' access to information simple and easy, (c) to conduct its functions openly and transparently, (d) to provide appropriate training and orientation to its staffs, (3) Public Body may use different national languages and mass media while publishing, broadcasting or making information public in accordance with Sub -Section 2 (a).

title: Updating and Publication of Information:
content: (1) Public Body has to keep update information related to them. (2) Public Body, as long as possible, has to update at least of twenty years old information from the commencement of this Act related to them in accordance with Sub-Section (1). Right to Information Act, 2007 (3) Public Body has to publish following information relating to their Body after making list thereof: (a) structure and nature of Body, (b) duties, responsibilities and powers of Body, (c) number of employees and working details of Body, (d) service to be provided by the Body, (e) branch and responsible officer of the service providing Body, (f) fee and time limit required for service, (g) decision making process and authority, (h) authority to hear appeal against decision (i) description of functions performed (j) name and designation of Chief and Information Officer (k) list of Acts, Rules, By Laws or guidelines (l) updated description of income and expenditures, financial transactions. (m) other particulars as prescribed. (4) Public Body shall have to update information in accordance with Sub- Section (3) within three months from the date of commencement of this Act and every three months afterwards and publish thereof.

title: Provision of Information Officer:
content: (1) Public Body will arrange for an Information Officer for the purpose of disseminating information held in its office. (2) For the purpose of disseminating information in accordance with Sub- Section (1), the Chief has to provide information held in the office regularly to the Information Officer. (3) Public Body shall set up an Information Section for the purpose of disseminating information as per necessity.

title: Procedures of Acquiring Information:
content: Right to Information Act, 2007 (1) Nepali Citizen, who is interested to obtain any information under this Act, shall submit an application before concerned Information Officer by stating reason to receive such information. (2) If an application is received in accordance with Sub-Section (1), Information Officer should provide the information immediately if the information by its nature could be provided immediately and has to provide within fifteen days from the date of application if the information by its nature could not be provided immediately. (3) If information cannot be provided immediately in accordance with Sub- Section (2), Information Officer should instantly give a notice with reason to the applicant. (4) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sub-Section (3), if information which is requested is related to security of life of any person, the information officer should provide information within Twenty Four hours of such request. (5) Information Officer has to provide information in the format as demanded by the applicant as much as possible. (6) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sub-Section (5), if any possibility subsist that the source of information may be damaged or destroyed or spoilt if it is provided in the format as requested by the applicant, the Information Officer shall provide such information in appropriate format with stating reason thereof. (7) If any person submitted an application to study or observe written document, materials or activities in accordance with Sub-Section (1), the Information Officer will provide a reasonable time to the applicant for the study and observation of such written document, materials or activities. (8) While examining the application received in accordance with Sub- Section (1), it is found that the information demanded by the applicant is not related to such Body, the Information Officer should give notification to the applicant immediately. Right to Information Act, 2007

title: Fee for information:
content: (1) Applicant has to pay fee as prescribed while requesting information in accordance with Section 7. Provided that, the fees shall be in accordance with the provision of prevalent laws, if different fees are prescribed for any specific information. (2) While determining the fee in accordance with Sub-Section (1) that will be based on the actual cost of providing information. (3) If the fee prescribed in accordance with Sub-Section (2) is deemed more than actual price, the concerned person shall make appeal before the Commission. (4) While examining the appeal in accordance with Sub-Section (3), the commission may order to review the fee if it is found in contrary to the Sub-Section (2).

title: Complaint shall be made:
content: (1) If Information Officer do not provide information, deny to provide information, partially provides information, provides wrong information or does not provide information by stating that the applicant is not stakeholder, the concerned person shall make a complaint to Chief within (7) days from the date of information denied or partial information received. (2) While investigating the complaint received in accordance with Sub- Section (1), the Chief shall order the Information Officer to provide information as demanded by applicant if it is found that the information was denied or partially provided or wrong information was provided and the Information Officer has to provide information to the concerned applicant if such order is issued. (3) While doing investigation in accordance with Sub-Section (2), if it is found that the Information Officer denied to provide information or partially provided the information knowingly or with malafide intention or Right to Information Act, 2007 provided wrong information, the Chief may take departmental action against such Information Officer. (4) While investigating in accordance with Sub-Section (2), it is found that the information cannot be provided; the Chief shall make a decision accordingly and provide a notice stating the reasons to the applicant.

title: Appeal shall be made:
content: (1) A person who is aggrieved by the decision of the Chief made in accordance with Sub-Section (4) of Section 9 shall appeal before the Commission within Thirty Five (35) days of the notice of decision received. (2) Commission shall summon and take statement of the concerned Chief or Information Officer, order to submit written document, take statement of witness and evidence or demand any document from Public Body while investigating and deciding the appeal received in accordance with Sub-Section (1). (3) While investigating and deciding the appeal in accordance with Sub- Section (2), the Commission shall do the following: a. By giving time, may order the concerned Chief to provide information to the appellant without fee, if appeal is found reasonable. b. Dismiss the appeal if it is found not reasonable. (4) The Commission has to give final verdict on the appeal within sixty days of appeal submission. (5) Other procedures to be followed by the commission during appeal pursuant to this Section shall be as prescribed. Chapter- Three Provision Regarding Commission

title: Provision Regarding Commission:
content: Right to Information Act, 2007 (1) An independent National Information Commission will be established for the protection, promotion and practice of right to information. (2) A Chief Information Commissioner and two other Information Commissioners will be in the commission. (3) In order to appoint Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners, there will be a committee comprised as follows: a. The Speaker – Chairperson b. Minister or State Minister for Information and Communication – Member c. President, Federation of Nepalese Journalists – Member (4) The Government of Nepal on the recommendation of the Committee under Sub-Section (3), will appoint a Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners; while appointing in this way, at least one female will have to be included. (5) The Committee in accordance with Sub-Section (3) will follow inclusive principles as much as possible while recommending for appointment of Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners. (6) The procedures of recommendation in accordance with Sub-Section (3) will be as determined by the Recommendation Committee itself.

title: Qualifications:
content: To be appointed for the position of the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners should have following qualification: a. Nepali citizen, b. having received at least Bachelor Degree From a recognized University, c. having fifteen years of working experience in the field of Mass communication, law justice, public administration, information technology or management.

title: Disqualifications:
content: Right to Information Act, 2007 The following person will be disqualified for being appointed in the position of Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners: a. Not having the qualification in accordance with Section 12, b. Convicted by a court on morally turpitude criminal offence, c. Incumbent employee of Government and Public institution, d. Incumbent in any political position, e. disqualified to be appointed under the prevailing laws.

title: Term of Office:
content: (1) The term of office of the Chief Information Commissioner and the Information Commissioners will be for 5 years and s/he shall not be re- appointed in the same Post. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sub-Section (1), the Information Commissioner shall be re-appointed in the post of Chief Information Commissioner under the provision of term of office stated in the same Sub- Section. (3) The recommendation committee in accordance with Sub-Section (3) of Section 11 has to make recommendation for new appointment one month prior to the expiry of the term of Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners.

title: Post to be Vacated:
content: The post the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioner shall be considered vacant under the following conditions: a. In case of his/her death, b. In case of s/he has completed the age 65, c. In case s/he tendered resignation to the Prime Minister, d. In case his/her term of office is completed, e. In case of s/he is convicted by the court on morally turpitude criminal offence, f. In case of he is removed from the post in accordance with Section 16. Right to Information Act, 2007

title: May Remove From Office:
content: If the meeting of the Legislature-Parliament endorse the recommendation of the information and communication related committee of the Legislature-Parliament, with the two third majority of meeting presented by at least two third members out of total members, for removing Chief Information Commissioner or Information Commissioner by the reason that s/he is not fit to hold office for the reason of incompetence or misbehavior or not carrying out the duties honestly, such Chief Information Commissioner or Information Commissioner will be removed from his/her office. Provided that, the Chief Information Commissioner or Information Commissioner charged with such accusation will not be denied for reasonable opportunity of clarification.

title: Provision Regarding the Conditions of Service:
content: The remuneration, condition of service and facilities for Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioner will be as prescribed.

title: Oath of Office:
content: Before taking charge of the office, the Chief Information Commissioner will take the oath of office before the Prime Minister and the Information Commissioner before the Chief Information Commissioner respectively in the format as laid down in Schedule.

title: Functions, Duties and Powers of the Commission:
content: In addition to the functions, duties and powers stated elsewhere in this Act, the functions, duties and powers of the Commission will be as follows: a. To observe and study the records and documents of public importance held in Public Bodies, Right to Information Act, 2007 b. To order for maintaining list of information related with document and records held in such Body orderly, c. To order concerned Public Body to make information public for citizen's notification, d. To prescribe timeframe and order concerned Public Body to provide information demanded by applicant within such timeframe. e. To order concerned party to fulfill liabilities in accordance with this Act. f. To provide necessary suggestions and recommendations to Government of Nepal and various other bodies related to information and communications regarding the protection and maintenance of right to information. g. To issue other appropriate orders regarding the protection, promotion and exercise of right to information.

title: Power Delegation:
content: The commission may delegate any of the functions, duties or powers except the power to hear and decide on appeal under Section 9, to the Chief Information Commissioner, Information Commissioner or any other body or official, subject to prescribed terms and conditions by this Act.

title: Office of the Commission:
content: The central office of the Commission will be placed in Kathmandu Valley and the Commission shall open its offices in various places of the country as per its necessity.

title: Staffs of the Commission:
content: (1) Necessary number of staffs will be there at the Commission. (2) The Government of Nepal will provide staffs necessary for the Commission.

title: Expenditure of the Commission:
content: (1) The Government of Nepal will arrange budget necessary for the Commission. Right to Information Act, 2007 (2) The Commission shall also obtain financial resources necessary for it from other sectors after getting prior permission of the Government of Nepal.

title: Cooperate with the Commission:
content: Public Bodies have to provide necessary cooperation in the activities of Commission.

title: Annual Report:
content: (1) The commission will have to submit Annual Report on its activities to the Legislature-Parliament through Prime Minister each year. (2) The Commission will publish the Annual Report in accordance with Sub- Section (1) publicly for the purpose of public notification.

title: Contact With the Government of Nepal:
content: The Commission should maintain contact with the Government of Nepal through the Ministry of Information and Communication. Chapter- Four Provision Regarding Protection of Information

title: Provision Regarding Classification of Information:
content: (1) For the protection of the information related to Sub-Section (3) of Section 3, held in public Body, there will be a committee as following to classify the information in policy level. a. Chief Secretary of the Government of Nepal- Chairperson b. Secretary of Relevant Ministry – Member c. Expert of concerned subject assigned by the Chief of Office or Chairperson – Member (2) The Committee in accordance with Sub-Section (1), regarding the classification of information under Section 3 (3), has to inform the Right to Information Act, 2007 Commission by determining the number of years the information should be kept confidential and method for the protection of information. (3) Person who is not satisfied with the recommendation made by the Committee under Sub-Section (2) may appeal before the Commission for review by demanding such information to be made public. (4) During the course of reviewing of an appeal in accordance with Sub- Section (3), if the Commission finds that certain information need not be kept confidential, shall order to make such information public. (5) The information classified in accordance with the Sub-section (2) may be kept confidential for maximum period of 30 years, according to the nature of the information. (6) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sub-section (5), the Committee should review in every ten years that any information classified as confidential is necessary to keep it up confidential or not. (7) While reviewing in accordance with Sub-Section (6), the Committee, if finds necessary to keep such information confidential for additional period, may decide the duration and classify as confidential for that period or may classify as non-confidential if finds not necessary to keep confidential.

title: Protection of Information:
content: (1) Public Body shall protect the information of personal nature held in for preventing unauthorized publication and broadcasting. (2) Personal information held in public Body, except in following situation, shall not be used without written consent of concerned person. a. In case of preventing a serious threat to life and body of any person or public health or security. b. If required to be disclosed in accordance with prevailing laws. c. If related to investigation of offence of corruption.

title: Protection of Whistleblower:
content: Right to Information Act, 2007 (1) It shall be a responsibility of employee of Public Body to provide information on any ongoing or probable corruption or irregularities or any deed taken as offence under the prevailing laws. (2) It shall be the duty of information receiver to make the identity of whistleblower in accordance with Sub-Section (1) confidential. (3) No harm or punishment is done to bear any legal responsibility to the whistleblower for providing information in accordance with Sub-Section (1). (4) If any punishment or harm is done to the whistleblower against the Sub- Section (3), the whistleblower may complaint, along with demand for compensation, before the commission for revoking such decision. (5) While investigating the complaint in accordance with Sub-Section (4), the Commission may order including to revoke the decision of removal from the office if he is removed from office and for the compensation if any damages occurred to the whistleblower.

title: Providing Personal Information:
content: (1) Concerned Body will have to provide information related with the public post to the concerned person, if any person demands information of during his service in the public Body. (2) Information have to be provided to the concerned person if a person demands for information related with him held in Public Body. (3) The procedures for demanding and acquiring information in accordance with Sub-Section (1) will be as stated in Section 7. (4) Fees will be in accordance with Section 8 for acquiring information under the Sub-Section (1).

title: Information not to be Misused:
content: (1) Any person who obtains any information from any public Body should not misuse the information by not using it for the purpose that was considered. Right to Information Act, 2007 (2) The concerned Public Body may complain to the Commission against any person who misuse the information against Sub-Section (1). Chapter- Five Provision Regarding Punishment and Cooperation

title: Punishment:
content: (1) If the Commission finds that Chief of public Body or Information Officer has held back information without any valid reason, refused to part with information, provided partial or wrong information or destroyed information; the Commission may impose a fin to such Chief or Information Officer from Rupees 1,000 to 25,000 and if such Chief or Information Officer is in a Post to be punished by Department, it may write to the concerned Body for departmental action. (2) If the Chief of public Body or Information Officer delay to provide information which has to be provided on time without reason, they shall be punished with a fine Rupees 200 per day for the information is delayed to provide. (3) If the Commission writes to the concerned Body for Departmental action in accordance with Sub-section (1), the Public Body will have to take Departmental action against that Chief or Information Officer within three months and notify the Commission thereon. (4) The Commission may impose a fine between NRS 5000 to 25000 considering that seriousness of misuse of information if any person is found misusing the information acquired from public Body instead of using it for purpose it was obtained for. (5) The Commission may impose a fine up to Rupees 10,000 to the concerned person in case its decision or order in accordance with this Act is not obeyed.

title: Compensation:
content: Right to Information Act, 2007 (1) If any person incur losses and damages due to not providing information, denying to provide information, providing partial or wrong information or destroy the information by the Chief or Information Officer of Public Body, such person may appeal before the Commission for compensation within three months from the date of not acquiring information, acquiring partial or wrong information or destroyed information. (2) If the application in accordance with Sub-Section (1) is found reasonable after the investigation, the Commission by considering the actual loses, may compensate the applicant from the concerned Body with reasonable amount.

title: Appeal:
content: Any person not satisfied with the decision rendered by the Commission in accordance with Section 32 may appeal before the Appellate Court within thirty five days of decision received. Chapter- Six Miscellaneous

title: Information may be Corrected:
content: (1) If anyone believed that the information in Public Body on a particular subject is wrong, s/he may appeal before the concerned Chief along with necessary evidences for the correction of the information. (2) The Chief shall conduct necessary investigation regarding the application in accordance with Sub-Section (1) and if the information held in such Body is found wrong during the course of investigation, s/he should inform the applicant within seven days from the date of application received by correcting thereon.

title: Save to Works done with Good Faith:
content: Right to Information Act, 2007 Notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, no case shall be filed and no punishment shall be imposed against the Chief or Information Officer for his works regarding the information dissemination done in good faith.

title: To be in accordance with this Act:
content: All the matters written in this Act will be carried out in accordance with this Act, whereas other matters will be dealt in accordance with prevalent laws.

title: Right to Make Rules:
content: The Government of Nepal by consulting with the Commission shall make necessary rules to implement the objectives of this Act. Right to Information Act, 2007 Schedule (Related to Section 18) Oath I .......................... hereby faithful to the state and the people promise with truth and trust/take the oath in the name of God that highly respecting the will expressed by the people through the people's movement that Nepal's state authority and sovereignty is to be vested only on the people, professing allegiance to the constitution of Nepal and laws of the land, I will carry out my responsibilities with honesty and without any fear, sycophancy, partiality, malice or greed, by honoring citizen's right to information and for the effective implementation and practice of laws pertaining to right to information. If the owner of a motor vehicle imported by a citizen of Nepal for personal use with the enjoyment of value added tax exemption dies and the motor vehicle has to be transmitted to the husband or wife of the owner of motor vehicle, the value added tax shall not be levied on such a motor vehicle on the basis of the approval of the Department.

title: Penalties:
content: 26(1) In cases where any person commits any of the following offenses, the Tax Officer may impose fines as follows:- (a) For breach of Sub-sections (1) or (2) of Section 10, tax payable for each tax period plus Ten Thousand Rupees. (b) For breach of Sub-section (5), (6) or (7) of Section 10, One Thousand Rupees for each time of breach. www.lacommission.gov.np www.lacommission.gov.np (c) For breach of Sub-sections (1) and (4) of Section 14, the amount of tax payable plus Two Thousand Rupees. (d) For breach of Section 15, the amount of tax collected plus cent percent of that amount. (e) For failure to maintain up-to-date accounts of transaction pursuant to Sub-section (1) of Section 16, Ten Thousand Rupees and for refusal of inspection of the books of accounts, Five Thousand Rupees for each time. (f) For breach of Sub-section (2) of Section 16, upto Five Thousand Rupees. (g) For breach of Sub-section (3) or (4) of Section 16, Ten Thousand Rupees. (h) For breach of provision of Section 18, One Thousand Rupees per tax period or 0.05 percent of the tax payable per day whichever is higher. (i) For obstructing to carry out the functions under Section 23, Five Thousand Rupees for each time of obstruction. (j) For under invoicing the sales price Two Thousand Rupees for each invoice or the fine imposed under Sub-section (2) whichever is higher. Provided that, if the office thinks appropriate, it may purchase or cause to purchase the goods that are under invoiced, as prescribed. (k) For breach of Act and Rules made there under Ten Thousand Rupees, for each time of breach. Amended by First Amendment. www.lacommission.gov.np www.lacommission.gov.np (2) If a person commits any of the following offences, a Tax Officer may impose a fine not exceeding twice the amount of tax or an imprisonment up to Six months, or penalize with both the fine and the imprisonment: (a) Preparing false accounts, invoices or other documents; (b) Committing a fraud or an evasion of tax; (c) If an unregistered person acts as if he/she were a registered person; (d) Carrying out a transaction by infringing Section 30.

title: Power equal to a Court:
content: For the purpose of this Act, a Tax Officer may issue a summons, record the statements of persons, receive evidence and cause to submit documents in the same manner as a court is empowered. 31A.Power to assess tax by taking action again: (1) In cases where, before tax is assessed, it appears from the information received by the Director General that any action relating to assessment of tax is about to be irregular or has been irregular, the Director General may, by executing a memorandum clearly setting out the reasons thereof, give direction to the concerned Tax Officer to assess tax by taking action again or order to any other officer to carry out that act. Inserted by First Amendment. www.lacommission.gov.np www.lacommission.gov.np (2) In cases where a taxpayer makes an application, within Thirty Five days of receipt of the tax assessment order, claiming that tax liability has increased because of failure of the Tax Officer to observe any matter required to be observed in assessing tax or irregularity or recklessness committed by that Officer, and where that matter appears to be true upon investigation, the Director General may, by executing a memorandum setting out the reasons thereof, cancel the tax assessment order and order to reassess tax. In cases where an order is so issued for reassessment of tax, the Director General has to give information thereof to the Government of Nepal, Ministry of Finance within Three days. Provided that, if an appeal has already been made pursuant to Section 32, the Director General shall not issue an order pursuant to this Sub-section. (3) The taxpayer who makes an application pursuant to Sub- section (2) has to pay undisputed amount of tax, out of the amount of tax assessed, and furnish a deposit in a sum equal to the amount of tax in controversy and Fifty percent of the fine or furnish bank guarantee for such amount. (4) In cases where the tax liability decreases because of tax assessment by the Tax Officer with recklessness or ulterior motive, the Director General may, within Four years from the date of initial assessment of tax, give order to amend such tax assessment order.

title: Appeal:
content: An appeal may be filed at the Revenue Tribunal within thirty- five days against a tax assessment or a penalty order made by the Tax Office or an order made by the Director General under Section 30.

title: Security To be Deposited:
content: 28In making an appeal to the Revenue Tribunal pursuant to this Act, one has to pay undisputed amount of tax, Amended by First Amendment. www.lacommission.gov.np www.lacommission.gov.np out of the amount of tax assessed, and furnish a deposit in a sum equal to the amount of tax in controversy and Fifty percent of the fine or furnish a bank guarantee for such amount.

title: Delegation of power:
content: (1) Except the authority of tax assessment and penalties, a Tax Officer may delegate all or any of the authority conferred on him/her by this Act to his/her subordinate staff. (2) No authority specified in this Act to be exercised by the Director General shall be delegated.

title: Serving of Notice:
content: Any notice, order or document issued by the Director General or the Tax Officer shall be considered to have been served on a taxpayer after the procedure, as prescribed, has been completed.

title: Tax Officers to be Punished:
content: If the Director General decides that a tax assessment was so made maliciously or negligently so that the tax amount was reduced or increased, he/she shall initiate a Departmental action against the assessing Tax Officer in accordance with the law related with his/her conditions of service. Provided that, a reasonable opportunity shall be given to the Tax Officer to submit his/her clarification.

title: No Responsibility for the act Carried out with Good Faith:
content: Notwithstanding anything contained in other places of this Act, a Tax Officer shall not be individually responsible for the act he/she had carried out in pursuance of discharging his/her duties with good faith.

title: Reward:
content: (1) A person who provides information with evidence showing that a taxpayer has evaded or attempted to evade all or some portions of tax shall be awarded as reward the amount equal to Twenty per cent of the amount of tax recovered on the basis of that information. 30Decision to award such reward shall be made by the Director General. (2) If there is more than one informer under Sub-section (1), the allotment of reward between or among them shall be as determined by the Director General.

title: Power to Frame Rules:
content: Government of Nepal may frame Rules to implement the objectives of this Act.

title: Addition and Alteration in the Schedules:
content: Government of Nepal may make required changes in the schedules by publishing a Notification in the Nepal Gazette. Inserted by First Amendment. www.lacommission.gov.np www.lacommission.gov.np

title: Prevailing Laws to Prevail in Other:
content: This Act and Rules framed thereunder shall prevail to the extent of the provisions, and in other cases other prevailing laws shall prevail.

title: I feel honour to present the budget for the fiscal year 2025/26 in this esteemed session of the Federal Parliament, the highest representative institution of the sovereign Nepali people.
On this occasion, I offer heartfelt tributes to the brave martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the movements for the abolition of monarchy and the establishment of a federal democratic republic.
content: I express my sincere respect to the esteemed leaders who played a leading role in those movements and to the sisters and brothers who contributed from their respective capacities.

title: With the promulgation of the Constitution of Nepal by the Constituent Assembly, the main agenda of Nepali politics has been changed.
content: The revised agenda has been guiding us to move forward at a rapid pace toward development, prosperity, social justice and socialism based on democratic values, in line with the national aspirations of a Prosperous Nepal, Happy Nepali.

title: However, in recent years, we have the bitter experience of the country's political situation becoming unexpectedly unstable, which has created an adverse effect on service delivery, good governance, and the pace of development, as well as making it challenging to address the needs of the nation and the expectations of the people.
Our own experience has shown that with appropriate policies and political stability, the country can be taken forward towards development, prosperity, and social justice.
content: We also have evidence that an average economic growth rate of 7.7 percent was achieved over a three-year period for the first time in history, after the promulgation of the constitution by the Constituent Assembly.

title: Based on this experience, the current government has been formed with the determination to ensure political stability, and accelerate economic and social development.
content: This government was formed under the leadership of two major political parties who have proud history and broad public support, and who have been playing a leading role in national politics. It is clear that there is no other favorable option for political stability and development within the limits of the current parliament's mathematical calculations. Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson, Now, I would like to briefly mention the current status of the economy.

title: When the current government was formed, the macroeconomic indicators clearly indicated that the economy was under pressure.
content: With the continuous efforts, the economy has moved towards a positive trajectory. The economic growth rate was 3.7 percent last year and is projected to be 4.6 percent in the current fiscal year. While the industry, construction, wholesale and retail trade sectors had negative growth rates in the last fiscal year, all sectors of the economy are projected to have positive growth rates in the current fiscal year. Notable growth rates are projected to be achieved in electricity, transportation and storage, and financial and insurance services.

title: By the end of mid-May in the current fiscal year, an additional 339 MW of electricity have been generated.
content: As of mid-May 2025, the number of tourist arrivals has increased by 13 percent compared to the same period of last year, reaching 923 thousand.

title: The year-on-year consumer inflation rate was 4.6 percent when the government assumed office whereas it is confined to 3.4 percent by the month of mid-April in the current fiscal year.
content: While the per capita gross domestic product was USD 1,443 last year, it is estimated to reach USD 1,496 in the current fiscal year.

title: In the first nine months of the current fiscal year, the current account has recorded a surplus of Rs.
content: 210 billion. The balance of payments surplus is Rs. 346 billion. The total foreign exchange reserves have reached USD 17.63 billion in the first nine months of the current fiscal year which was USD 15.27 billion at the end of the previous fiscal year.

title: In the first nine months of the current fiscal year, merchandise import has increased by 12.2 percent, while export has surged by 65.2 percent.
content: Additionally, remittance inflow has increased by 10 percent, reaching Rs. 1,191 billion.

title: The credit growth rate of banks and financial institutions was 5.8 percent last year whereas it is increased by 7.1 percent during the first nine months of the current fiscal year.
content: In the same period, deposits in banks and financial institutions have increased by 5.7 percent.

title: The average base rate of commercial banks was at 8.5 percent in mid-April of the previous year and it is maintained at 6.3 percent in mid-April 2025.
content: The decline in interest rate and the availability of sufficient loanable financial resources in banks and financial institutions have created a favorable environment for the expansion of private investment. The NEPSE index reached 2,662 in mid-April 2025 which was 2,025 in mid-April, 2024.

title: The revised estimate of the total government expenditure is Rs.
content: 1,662.37 billion in the current fiscal year, which is 89.4 percent of the allocation. The revised estimate for recurrent expenditure is 88.5 percent and for capital expenditure is 83.4 percent, and for financing is 97.6 percent of the allocation.

title: Revenue mobilization is estimated to increase by 17.1 percent, totaling Rs, 1,267.39 billion in fiscal year 2024/25.
content: On foreign assistance, the revised estimate is Rs. 34.89 billion in grants and Rs. 169.6 billion in loans to be mobilized.

title: For the current fiscal year, domestic borrowing was estimated at Rs.
content: 330 billion, of which Rs. 300.6 billion had been mobilized by mid-May, 2025.

title: I have already submitted Economic Survey 2024/25 that includes detail status of key indicators and statistics of Nepal’s economy, ministry-wise progress report and the financial status of public enterprises to this esteemed parliament.
content: Even though economic indicators are improving, Nepal’s economy has not been able to be free from the structural challenges and past weaknesses. Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson, Please allow me to describe the existing major challenges of national economy.

title: The country has been listed on the increased monitoring list for anti-money laundering due to lack of adequate legal provisions in a timely manner, and effective investigation and prosecution.
Agricultural productivity remains low, and farming remains unattractive to the youth as the expected improvement did not materialize in the traditional farming systems.
content: The limited use of innovation and technology, low productivity, and high production cost have adversely affected the manufacturing sector to contribute to national income as anticipated. A decline in aggregate demand has hindered the industrial sector to operate at full capacity. Investment in physical infrastructure has not been adequately reflected in the expansion of economic activities, hence failed to contribute to growth in production as desired. The adverse effect of climate change is increasing in agriculture, water supply, irrigation, and related sectors. Inadequate digital infrastructure has slowed the pace of development of digital economy. The country’s labor market and the skills of its human resources remain mismatched. The necessary manpower in the industrial and construction sectors is being supplied from abroad. The lack of generating sufficient employment opportunities domestically has led to worrisome trend of overseas migration both in skilled and semi-skilled labor. The proportion of the population living below the poverty line still remains high.

title: The private sector’s contribution to gross fixed capital formation of the nation has not increased as expected.
content: Innovative financing instruments developed for de-risking investment have not been effectively utilized. The flow of financial resources to manufacturing sector has not been adequate. There are challenges to enhance the effectiveness of regulatory bodies and to minimize the financial risks. Although Nepal’s first-ever sovereign credit rating yielded relatively favorable results, the benefits of this outcome are yet to be realized. Despite policy and legal reforms, foreign capital and technology have not been attracted as expected.

title: Due to the inability to expand and diversify exports, high trade deficit persists.
content: The import of consumable goods is high due to weak production capacity. The expected benefits from service exports, particularly in tourism and information technology, have not been fully realized. There is a challenge in sustainably maintaining external sector stability, which heavily relies on remittances.

title: Revenue saving for development is declining.
content: The sources of income are diminishing. Existing revenue structure faces challenge to make it broader, sustainable, and based on domestic production. Allocative efficiency has not been achieved. While recurrent expenditure remains high, it is becoming challenging to finance capital expenditure through conventional sources. Weak implementation capacity has resulted in cost and time overruns for project completion. Due to lack of appropriate resource management, there is an increasing risk that development programs and projects will remain limited to mere announcements. The rising volume of public debt poses an additional challenge to maintaining debt sustainability.

title: The lack of professionalization in public administration has hindered the anticipated improvement in the quality of service delivery.
content: The realization of good governance is challenging due to delays in public service, lack of accountability, traditional decision- making processes, and weak inter-agency coordination. Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson, I hereby present the following commitments to address above mentioned challenges and to make the economy dynamic:

title: Enhancing the credibility of the economy by delisting the country ahead of schedule from the increased monitoring list regarding money laundering has become a key agenda for the government.
content: The encouraging outcome of the first sovereign credit rating will be leveraged to mobilize external capital, while additional economic reform programs will be pursued to achieve a higher rating.

title: The private sector has been encouraged by the legal reforms introduced through ordinances to boost private sector confidence and create a conducive investment climate.
content: Public investments will be focused on high-return areas, attracting private capital and technology to promote exponential growth in economic activities. The private sector will be established as a key driver of economic prosperity by further advancing policy, legal, and procedural reforms in areas that contribute significantly to economic growth. The Report of the High-Level Economic Reform Advisory Commission, 2025, will be implemented gradually.

title: Resource will be diversified to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030 and to address potential investment shortfalls following Nepal’s graduation to a developing country status in 2026.
content: Revenue administration will be made professional and the tax system will be strengthened. Public debt will be mobilized in high-return sectors. Top emphasis will be given for the implementation of priority and result- oriented projects by curtailing inappropriate projects. Innovative and feasible instruments of alternative finance will be used to fill the gap in development finance.

title: Emphasis will be given on improving the trade balance by boosting exports of competitive goods and services and promoting domestic production of consumer goods.
content: Skilled Nepali professionals working abroad will be encouraged to return and engage in entrepreneurship and self-employment within the country. Top priority will be given to generate youth-oriented employment opportunities promoting innovation and entrepreneurship.

title: The Government is firmly committed to achieving further progress, bringing about positive changes in the lives of the people, overcoming all forms of despair, and instilling hope in the general public based on the positive outcomes achieved since the formation of the present government.
content: This budget has been formulated with the primary objective of expanding the economy and creating economic opportunities.

title: I have formulated the budget on the basis of the list of power enshrined in the Constitution of Nepal, periodic plan, the government’s common resolution and policy commitments, the Government of Nepal’s policies and programs endorsed by this esteemed Parliament, the views expressed by honourable members regarding the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, as well as suggestions received from parliamentary thematic committees, the private sector, the academic community, and the general public.
content: Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson, Please allow me to present the objectives and priorities of the budget for the upcoming fiscal year. The objectives of the budget are as follows: (a) To alleviate poverty by achieving high, sustainable, and broad-based economic growth. (b) To generate employment by promoting entrepreneurship and expanding public and private investment, (c) To enhance economic efficiency by increasing the use of modern technology, (d) To maintain social justice through social protection and development, and (e) To promote quality public service and good governance. The priorities of the budget are as follows: (a) Enhancement of entrepreneurship, employment, production, and productivity, (b) Expansion of investment in yielding, quality physical infrastructure, (c) Quality improvement in social sector, (d) Ensurance of balanced development and social security, and (e) Citizen-friendly services, corruption control, and governance reform. Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson, Please allow me to present the details related to fiscal transfer as per Article 60 of the Constitution of Nepal.

title: Based on the recommendation of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission, I have provisioned to transfer Rs.
content: 60.66 billion to the provinces and Rs. 88.97 billion to the local levels under fiscal equalization grants. I have allocated Rs. 30.35 billion for provinces and Rs. 211.46 billion for local levels, totalling Rs. 241.81 billion as conditional grants.

title: For the implementation of infrastructure project, I have allocated Rs.
content: 3.28 billion to the provinces and Rs. 10.06 billion to the local levels as complementary grants. Similarly, Rs. 3.27 billion is allocated for the provinces and Rs. 9.78 billion for the local levels as special grants. Arrangements have been made to transfer conditional, supplementary, and special grants based on performance.

title: It is estimated that Rs.
content: 165 billion will be transferred to the provinces and local levels through revenue sharing. It is projected that Rs. 582.83 billion will be transferred to provinces and local levels including revenue sharing and grants in the upcoming fiscal year. I now present the sectoral programs and allocations of the budget. Modernization in Agriculture: Transformation in the Economy

title: The production and productivity will be increased by commercialization and mechanization of agriculture sector.
content: The consumption of locally produced healthy and nutritious food will be promoted. Food sovereignty will be ensured. Excess labor force dependent on agriculture sector will be transformed to productive sectors.

title: Cultivable land will be utilized at most through collective, cooperative, and private firms.
content: Concrete programs will be implemented to achieve self-sufficiency in production of major food grains, vegetables, fruits, dairy, and meat products.

title: I have allocated Rs.
content: 3.50 billion to provide capital subsidies and concessions for irrigation, fertilizers, seeds, and technology in 21 super zones and 206 zones of agriculture and livestock under the National Agriculture Modernization Program. This program will expand the scope of cultivation area of 15 crops across 4,850 hectares using advanced techniques. Irrigation facilities will be extended to an additional 6 thousand hectares of land by developing small-scale irrigation infrastructure. I have made an arrangement to provide capital grants for the operation of block at the provincial level and pocket at the local level.

title: The scope of currently operating zones and super zones will be expanded.
content: Arrangement will be made to provide grant facilities for commercial farming or livestock rearing conducted in equivalent areas designated as super zones or zones through private, collective, contract-based, or cooperatives.

title: Chaite Dhan (Spring paddy) cultivation promotion program will be implemented in 22 districts of the Terai and Inner Madhesh to achieve self-sufficiency in rice within two years.
content: I have anticipated that an additional 1.2 million metric tons of paddy will be produced from this program. I have allocated Rs. 330 million for construction of irrigation infrastructure for Chaite Dhan farming.

title: Cultivation of high-value crops will be promoted in 80 local levels of mid and high-
content: hilly districts in Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces. I have allocated Rs. 830 million for this purpose.

title: Supply of chemical fertilizer will be increased to 600 thousand metric tons.
content: I have allocated Rs. 28.82 billion for subsidy in chemical fertilizer. Necessary preparations will be arranged to establish a chemical fertilizer factory through the Investment Board. I have allocated Rs. 400 million for organic farming promotion program to enhance productivity while maintaining soil quality.

title: Agricultural production will be encouraged on arable fallow lands located along the Pushpalal Mid-Hilly Highway and the Madan Bhandari Highway.
content: I have allocated funds for the expansion of cash crops, livestock farming, high-value fruits, non-timber forest products, grass, and agroforestry systems under this initiative.

title: Minimum support price will be set for paddy, maize, wheat, sugarcane, coffee, and other products prior to 15 days of plantation time.
content: In case of limited market access of those products, necessary arrangements will be made to purchase agricultural products through the Food and Trading Company Limited. Advance purchase agreements for agricultural products will be established after plantation.

title: Arrangements will be made for mandatory quality and pesticide testing of food grains, vegetables, fruits, meat, and dairy products before they are sold in the market.
content: Rapid pesticide residue testing on fresh vegetables and fruits at wholesale market centers will be done, and in cases where the produce is found inedible, arrangements will be made for its immediate disposal. I have allocated necessary budget for the arrangement of additional manpower and equipment, and mobilization of mobile team for pesticide testing.

title: Soil testing camps through mobile teams will be conducted to improve soil fertility and encourage appropriate farming.
content: Programs will be implemented for the registration of local and indigenous seed crops and expansion of their cultivation.

title: To increase exports of organic fruits, vegetables, meat, and other high-value agricultural products, the quality of plant, food, and animal quarantine services and laboratories will be improved for attaining international accreditation.
Concessions will be provided on laboratory testing and organic certification fees for agricultural products.
content: Zoning and compartmentalization programs will be implemented in Sindhuli and Makwanpur districts to declare them as Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) free zones.

title: Control measures will be adopted to minimize crop damage caused by wild animals like monkeys, wild boars, and nilgais.
content: Cultivation of crops such as simal tarul (tapioca), turmeric, tea, coffee, ginger, and chili will be encouraged in the monkey prone areas. Floriculture will be promoted.

title: Youths will be attracted in agriculture sector by developing a robust ecosystem with land, agricultural inputs, insurance, purchase agreements, and market.
content: Agricultural research will be made result-oriented so that it will be aligned with country's climate and farming systems benefitting farmers. Private sector participation will be encouraged in research and development of quality seed varieties. Arrangement will be made for registration of intellectual property rights achieved from agriculture research.

title: Livestock farming and quality meat production in large-scale farms will be emphasized to boost export potential of meat.
content: Livestock productivity will be improved by carrying out 850 thousand artificial inseminations through breed improvement program. Fifty- five million doses of vaccines will be produced in the coming fiscal year to control livestock diseases and epidemic in livestock and poultry. I have allocated Rs. 850 million for this purpose.

title: In the upcoming fiscal year, 42.8 million fish fingerlings and 1 million fruit saplings will be distributed.
content: One million coffee seedlings will be distributed by establishing coffee nurseries in 20 high-potential local levels.

title: I have made an arrangement to maintain adequate food reserves in the National Food Security Reserve and the SAARC Food Bank.
content: Infrastructure for safe transportation, storage, and easier market access of agricultural products will be developed in co- investment of the government and the private sector. Arrangements will be made for improved supply chain and a strengthened agricultural market information system to benefit farmers from value chain.

title: Nine large agricultural markets currently under construction will be completed and operated.
content: Construction of modern infrastructure in Semlar, Rupandehi will be initiated for the collection, processing, marketing, and export promotion of agricultural products.

title: Export of black cardamom, tea, coffee, ginger, turmeric, orange, Akabare chili, Chhurpi (Dog chew), and dairy products will be promoted through quality standard setting, laboratory testing, and branding.
Small and medium-scale farmers’ access to crop and livestock insurance program will be expanded.
content: I have allocated Rs. 2.30 billion for subsidy in crops and livestock insurance premium. 54. “Kisan App” will be developed and SMS-based information service will be managed to provide regular updates on weather forecasts, crop prices, and availability of agricultural inputs.

title: I have allocated Rs.
content: 57.48 billion to the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development. Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation

title: The issues of landless Dalits, squatters, and unorganized settlers will be resolved permanently by amending land-related laws.
content: Land ownership registration certificates will be provided to 500 thousand families after collecting and verifying their land records within the upcoming fiscal year. No shortage of resources, means, and manpower will be allowed for this purpose.

title: The records of government and public land will be updated and preserved.
content: A policy will be adopted to prohibit leaving arable land fallow. Legal and institutional arrangements related to land banks will be made to utilize arable land. In the upcoming fiscal year, land banks will be established in at least one hundred local levels. Provision of contract agreement with local level will be made if any landowner wish to lease their land. An arrangement will be made for the registered land in the land bank to be obtained through a contract with the local level for commercial farming.

title: Land use plan will be formulated by classifying land use zones through local levels.
content: The surveying work using LiDAR technology will be expanded. The LiDAR survey data will also be used for feasibility studies and design purposes for infrastructure development projects. A network of national control points based on satellite technology will be strengthened to organize the surveying work.

title: The records of the land reform and land revenue, and survey offices will be digitized.
content: The land information system will be upgraded and expanded to all offices. The freezing and releasing process of land by banks, financial institutions and cooperatives will be made online.

title: The classification, merger and structural improvement of cooperative organizations will be carried out.
content: Saving and credit cooperatives will be effectively regulated by the National Cooperative Regulation Authority.

title: The deposits of up to 500 thousand in the cooperative organization will be secured through the Deposit and Credit Guarantee Fund.
content: I have arranged seed capital to establish a revolving fund for refunding the saving of depositor by auctioning assets of those persons who have misused cooperative funds. A cooperative loan recovery tribunal will be established. The assets and passports of the directors, officials and loan defaulters of the problematic cooperatives will be blocked.

title: Arrangements will be made to self-declare and update necessary information for state benefit identity card in every five-year.
content: This information will be linked to the National Identity Card System. Individuals who receive state benefit declaring false information will be prosecuted according to the law. I have allocated conditional grants to complete the data collection and identity cards distribution work within the upcoming fiscal year.

title: Targeted programs will be executed in coordination with the federal, provincial, and local levels to eradicate absolute poverty.
I have allocated Rs.7.49 billion to the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation.
content: Industry, Trade, and Investment Promotion

title: The contribution of the industrial sector to the national economy will be increased by enhancing industrial production and productivity.
content: Industrialization will be accelerated through policy stability, investment security, and sound industrial relations.

title: Legal, policy, and procedural reforms will be highly prioritized by improving the business environment to promote private investment, and generate employment.
content: Branding of goods and services will be carried out by promoting micro, cottage, small, and medium industries. Promotion of modern technology in the industry sector and implementation of the Industry 4.0 concept will be supported and facilitated.

title: Startup entrepreneurship based on innovation will be promoted to increase the number of job creator youths rather than job seekers.
content: Incubation centers will be operated in collaboration with the government, universities, and the private sector to foster entrepreneurial and business skills among Gen-Z. I have expanded the concessional loan program to support skill development, business scaling, marketing, and value chain participation for startup entrepreneurs. I have allocated Rs. 730 million to provide loans at three percent interest rate for this program.

title: The “Bhagat Sarbajit Entrepreneurship Development Program” will be implemented to create employment and income opportunities by preserving traditional skills, arts, and occupations of the Dalit community.
content: Production and marketing of the materials including gold, silver, bronze, copper, iron, leather, wood, and stone will be carried out by using modern technology. I have allocated Rs. 500 million for providing capital grants, concessional loans, and skill development training for this program.

title: The bonded warehouse facility will be provided to the industries exporting gold and silver jewelry.
content: Industries that receive a minimum of 50 percent of their export value as foreign currency in advance payment will be permitted to purchase an equivalent amount of gold and silver.

title: Public services related to industry and business will be made simple, accessible, and technology-friendly.
content: Arrangements will be made to carry out all procedures from company registration to exit through a single-window system.

title: Industries with approval to establish new industry in Special Economic Zones and industrial areas will be exempted from the rent for the first three years.
content: Monthly rent in Special Economic Zones will be reduced from Rs. 20 to Rs. 5 per square meter. Benefits equivalent to the industries in Special Economic Zones will be provided to the industries in industrial zones if they export more than thirty percent of their production.

title: Companies developing industrial zones will be provided the same benefits as hydropower production companies, and industries established within these industrial zones will be provided the same benefits as industries in Special Economic Zones.
content: The prescribed monthly rent for industrial zones will be reduced by 50 percent. I have allocated Rs. 1.55 billion for the construction of industrial infrastructure.

title: Industries operating within the Kathmandu Valley will be encouraged to relocate to industrial zones outside the valley in order to control pollution in the capital region.
content: I have made arrangements to provide land on lease free of cost, for such industries.

title: Laws related to land acquisition and land holding limit will be reviewed.
content: Provisions will be made to allow the purchase of land above the ceiling for industries, agricultural farms, and housing apartments. Arrangements will be made to allow the sale of housing and apartments which were built with approval but unsold due to land ceiling restrictions.

title: Nepal will be developed as a premier destination for foreign direct investment.
content: Investment promotion and double taxation avoidance agreements will be signed with potential countries for investment. Procedures for the inflow of foreign investment and profit repatriation will be simplified. Anchor investment policy will be adopted to attract foreign investment in national priority sectors.

title: Legal reforms will be carried out to strengthen Public-Private Partnership.
content: An automated one-stop service center will be established under the Investment Board. Provision of viability gap funding will be made to attract investment in the projects of the priority sector.

title: The Investment Board will be mandated to manage resources, select projects, and implement them in line with the Public-Private Partnership concept at the federal level along with the provincial and local levels.
content: A Public-Private Partnership Directorate will be established under the Investment Board for this purpose.

title: Legal provisions will be made to allow foreign investors, multinational companies, international institutions, and their branches to lease buildings or apartments for office or residential use.
Institutional capacity of the Investment Board will be strengthened.
content: Within fiscal year 2025/26, project development agreements worth Rs. 700 billion with the private sector will be made, and the construction of projects worth Rs. 400 billion will be initiated. I have allocated Rs. 740 million to the Investment Board.

title: Permission will be granted to Nepali entrepreneurs or companies to export semi processed materials and establish processing plants or sales branches abroad.
content: To facilitate this, legal provisions will be made to permit investment in foreign countries up to 25 percent of their annual export earnings. A provision will be made requiring at least 50 percent of the profit earned from such a business to be repatriated back into the country. The responsibility for approving investments made abroad will be assigned to the Investment Board.

title: Legal provisions will be made to allow Nepali citizens to receive sweat shares in return for providing technology or specialized knowledge or services to foreign companies.
The Industrial Park in Damak, Jhapa will be constructed, operated and managed under the Public-Private-Partnership through the Investment Board.
content: Modern industrial zones will be developed in Daiji (Kanchanpur), Naubasta (Banke), Lakshmipur (Dang), Motipur (Rupandehi), Shaktikhor (Chitwan), and Mayurdhap (Makwanpur) with private sector participation through the Investment Board. Special Economic Zones in Panchkhal and Simara will be operated in partnership with the private sector.

title: An export strategy targeting products with comparative and competitive advantage will be adopted.
content: Trade infrastructure development and technology transfer will be prioritized. “Make in Nepal and Made in Nepal” campaign will be conducted in collaboration with the private sector.

title: The Integrated Check Post in Bhairahawa and the dry port in Timure, Rasuwa will be completed and brought into operation.
content: Construction of a dry port in Dodhara-Chandani, Kanchanpur will be initiated.

title: An inventory of identified mineral resources from the geological study, including petroleum, copper, iron, magnesium, phosphorite, quartz, and precious stones, will be prepared.
content: Petroleum exploration in Dailekh will be completed, and commercial production will be commenced based on sample test reports. Petroleum exploration will be initiated in Palpa, Sunsari, and Dang. The feasibility study of rare earth metals will be carried out by selecting the capable researchers from the international community.

title: An international conference will be organized in fiscal year 2025/26 with the participation of mining experts to assess the potential for exploration, production, and marketing of mineral-based products in Nepal.
Private sector will be encouraged to participate in commercial production and marketing of natural and mineral-based products.
content: Arrangements will be made for the extraction and processing of mineral and river-based construction materials found environmentally and economically viable through environmental impact assessments, for domestic use and export.

title: Quality standards will be defined in line with international norms, and mutual recognition will be established with export destination countries.
content: Standardization and certification of products manufactured in Nepal will be made systematic and of high quality. The law related to protection of intellectual property will be updated to reflect current needs.

title: Facilitation for providing working capital loans in easy and accessible way to manufacturing, tourism, and construction industries, along with housing development companies will be done.
Smooth supply of food grains and salt will be ensured in remote and hilly areas.
content: Fuel storage capacity will be expanded to ensure a smooth supply. Arrangements will be made to blend bioethanol in order to control pollution and reduce petrol imports.

title: Expansion of the Amlekhgunj-Lothar petroleum pipeline and construction of storage site will be initiated.
content: Construction of the Siliguri-Charali cross-border petroleum pipeline and storage site will be initiated.

title: Malpractices such as black marketing, monopolies, syndicates, and the creation of artificial shortages will be controlled to maintain a clean, competitive, and consumer-
content: friendly market. Consumer court will be expanded to all provinces.

title: I have allocated Rs.
content: 10.14 billion to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. Tourism Infrastructure and Heritage Conservation

title: Nepal will be branded as a safe and attractive tourist destination through the development of infrastructure, expansion of quality services, and marketing.
content: Special promotional packages will be launched targeting tourists from the neighboring countries.

title: Tourist-centric services will be expanded in major destinations of eco-tourism, mountain and adventure tourism, and religious and cultural tourism.
content: Tourism promotion programs based on nature, culture, adventure, movies, wellness, and sports will be implemented. Welcome and Service Centers will be established at entry points targeting tourist arriving by land routes.

title: Private sector investment will be encouraged in the development of tourism infrastructure.
content: Development of jungle safari, trekking trails, and eco-tourism facilities in national parks, reserves, and protected areas will be emphasized. Arrangements will be made to lease the government-owned land, including forest areas for the construction of tourism infrastructure such as hill stations, hotels, lodges, and resorts.

title: Tourism promotion programs will be conducted in collaboration with the private sector and with the facilitation from the Nepal Tourism Board.
content: Safe and accessible trekking routes will be developed to promote tourism in the high hill and himalayan regions. Trekking routes will be operated along Shuklaphanta-Khaptad, Bardiya-Rara, Lumbini- Muktinath, Sauraha-Gosaikunda, Janakpurdham-Kalinchowk, Koshi Tappu- Sagarmatha, and Kechana-Pathibhara. Likewise, eco-tourism trails to Khaptad, Ramaroshan, Badimalika, Budhinanda, Rara, Swargadwari, and Muktinath will be developed. A reliable system for the safety and emergency rescue of trekkers and mountaineers will be arranged.

title: Hotels and resorts will be granted income tax and electricity tariff exemptions equivalent to those provided to manufacturing industries.
content: Legal provisions will be introduced to provide incentive through service charges to workers employed in tourism businesses such as hotels, motels, restaurants, and jungle safaris.

title: Infrastructure will be developed at major religious, cultural, and tourism destinations such as Sagarmatha, Pashupatinath, Lumbini, Janakpurdham, Muktinath, Swargadwari, Rara, Khaptad.
content: A comprehensive Lumbini Master Plan will be prepared and implemented for the protection, development, and promotion of the Lumbini area. Sandhyakalin Sampada Marga (Evening heritage trails) will be developed in Swayambhunath, Hanumandhoka, Pashupatinath, and Boudhanath areas.

title: Development of tourism infrastructure will be emphasized in the attractive locations near the Pushpalal Mid-Hill Highway.
content: Private sector will be encouraged to carry out rafting and other tourism activities in major rivers including Karnali, Bheri, Gandaki, Trishuli, Koshi.

title: The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal will be strengthened institutionally by separating into regulatory and service providing agencies.
content: Necessary measures will be taken to delist Nepal from aviation safety concern list within the upcoming fiscal year. Domestic aviation services will be made safer and more accessible.

title: I have allocated Rs.
content: 4.15 billion to develop the Tribhuvan International Airport into a boutique airport by expanding the capacity for managing the increasing passenger traffic. The Pokhara International Airport will be developed as a tourism hub.

title: The Gautam Buddha International Airport will be operated with necessary facilities to make it cost-effective for tourists and migrant workers.
content: Special incentives will be provided to operate cargo services from this airport.

title: International airlines operating in Nepal will be encouraged to operate a fixed number of flights from Bhairahawa and Pokhara airports through additional facilities and incentives.
content: The construction process of Nijgadh International Airport will be initiated through the use of alternative development financing.

title: Capacity of Bhadrapur (Jhapa), Tarigaun (Dang), and Suketar (Taplejung) airports will be expanded.
content: Pre-preparatory work for the construction of a regional airport in Surkhet will be completed, and constructions work will be initiated. Detailed project reports will be prepared for Chuhandanda (Tehrathum), Ajaymeru (Dadeldhura), and Sagarmatha (Udayapur) airports. I have allocated Rs. 500 million for the development of domestic airport infrastructure.

title: Alternative utilization plans will be formulated for domestic airports with low traffic.
content: Such airports will be used for aviation training and adventure tourism activities such as paragliding, parachuting, ultralight, skydiving in partnership with the private sector. Economic and commercial feasibility will be considered as the main criteria for the construction and expansion of new domestic airports.

title: Ancient history, culture, and archaeological heritage of Nepal will be preserved.
content: Panini Knowledge Park will be established in Panena, Arghakhanchi in the memory of Rishi Panini, the founder of Sanskrit grammar. I have allocated budget for digital archiving of historically and archaeologically significant documents.

title: I have allocated Rs.
content: 13.28 billion to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation. Forest and Environment

title: Forest areas will be conserved and forest products will be utilized as national resources.
content: Forest areas will be utilized for commercial purposes and managed sustainably in a manner that does not adversely affect the environment and biodiversity.

title: The provision requiring re-measurement before cutting down the trees that have been previously measured while granting the right to forest area uses will be removed.
content: Withered and fallen trees will be collected and utilized.

title: Seasoning industries will be encouraged to increase quality production and consumption of domestic wood and wood-based products.
content: The establishment of Furniture and veneer industries will be encouraged in the vicinity of the Pushpalal Mid- Hill Highway.

title: Grasslands and water sources will be managed to conserve biodiversity and natural habitats of wildlife.
content: Community development, income generation, and employment programs will be implemented for residents of buffer zones. Buffer zones will be managed ensuring human-wildlife coexistence. Solar fencing with modern technology will be utilized for conservation and control of elephant’s natural corridors to prevent loss of life and property from wild elephant attacks.

title: Export promotion of herbs will be emphasized by carrying out production, collection, processing, lab certification, and marketing.
content: The production capacity of Herbs Production and Processing Company Limited will be enhanced by infrastructure development and improved management. I have allocated Rs. 200 million for this purpose.

title: Communities will be encouraged to plant and conserve fruits, herbs, and high-value plants in the community forests and the sides of national highways.
content: The Fruit Forest Program will be executed in collaboration with communities.

title: Integrated watersheds management will be implemented to make water cycles sustainable in Chure and Terai-Madhesh regions.
content: Conservation of gorges and wetlands, afforestation and natural restoration of forest, water retention and recharge related programs will be implemented. I have allocated Rs. 1.69 billion for these activities.

title: National parks, conservation areas, and forest areas will be utilized, and development projects will be implemented without adversely affecting the environment and biodiversity.
content: An arrangement will be made to deposit only one percent of the land management and tree nurturing costs into the Forest Development Fund for using forest areas in development projects implemented by the federal, provincial, and local levels.

title: Environmental Impact Assessment process will be made swift, simple, and easy.
content: A provision will be made to approve project site selection and environmental report simultaneously.
